correctness.rationale: Exact Hölder reduction with p=8/7 is reconstructible; positivity of maximizers holds for p>1 by epsilon-improvement; every reflection-symmetric Perron vector reduces to F(t) with unique max at t+t^8=1. Integer inequalities bracket its maximizer and strictly bound the fourth power by (161/250)^4. The positive integer witness (5,10,11,10) yields Q^4>(161/250)^4 S^7 and is a valid Rayleigh quotient. P2/P3 unique symmetry follows from AM-GM and strict concavity. The packaged verify.py replays exact certificates; no extrapolation from finite tests.

value.rationale: Network symmetry is a common simplifying assumption when allocating fixed conservation area. This sharp, smallest-order constructive failure forces analysts to search outside symmetric allocations even on a homogeneous four-patch corridor. It converts the issue into a rigorously strict local invasion-threshold gap, with an independent rational certificate rather than a numerical optimization artifact. Exact minimizer coordinates and other exponents are deliberately not claimed.
